title: long-tail burst smoother and compact trace serializer
author: Maya Chen
ci_status: pass (initial lint failure fixed by commit 3, full suite green on re-run)
description:
Motivation: Long-tail burst patterns in customer traffic cause noisy p95/p99 regressions in our inference profiling. Existing workload synthesizers either amplify bursts unrealistically or smooth them with heuristics that lose temporal locality. This PR introduces a deterministic long-tail burst smoother that preserves session-level locality while reducing artificial kernel coalescing, plus a compact trace serializer to reduce reporter storage overhead for high-resolution runs.

What this PR does: 1) Adds a new workload synthesizer (long_tail_smoother) that post-processes generated request streams and applies epoch-aware smoothing rules. The smoother uses a tunable 'burst_decay' kernel and epoch-resampling to maintain representative hot-paths while reducing microburst noise for stable baselines. 2) Implements a compact trace serializer (compact_trace_serializer) in Go that writes deduplicated event frames and an index table for fast downstream aggregation. The serializer targets our reporter pipeline and reduces disk usage by ~4x for high-frequency traces. 3) Integrates both pieces into the experiment harness and adds per-run metrics for 'smoothed_burst_ratio', 'residual_kv_hits', and 'trace_compaction_ratio'. 4) Adds unit and integration tests and updates the benchmark dashboard query templates.

Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked in ENG-4621 - [x] Unit tests for smoother edge cases - [x] Integration test exercising serializer in a 1k-request short-run - [x] CI linting and type checks - [x] Dashboard query updates and example run artifacts attached

Performance notes: In local and CI perf runs we see median throughput within 2% of the original generator, p95 reduced in noisy microburst scenarios by 18-27% (depending on sequence mix), and trace storage reduced by 3.6-4.5x. These numbers are in the PR run artifacts (perf/artifacts/77421).

Compatibility and rollout: The smoother is opt-in via harness flags (--smoother=long_tail, --burst-decay=0.75) so it will not affect existing baselines until we flip the default in a follow-up. Serializer is backward-compatible with the reporter pipeline; the legacy JSON trace writer remains available behind a flag.

Notes for reviewers: Pay attention to metric names and label cardinality; the serializer deduplicates frames based on a 128-bit hash, we need to be sure collision risk is acceptable for production-size runs. The PR intentionally keeps the hash seed configurable for replay determinism.

Release notes: Added an opt-in long-tail burst smoother for workload generation and a compact trace serializer to reduce reporter storage and speed up downstream aggregation.
